subtype: Approach: consulting a doctor for general preparation [Action]
passage:
Wednesday night

Today was the check-up. Finally.
For two months I'd been reading forums at midnight. One said eat this, another said never eat that. Keerthana's mother-in-law told her a list of rules that contradicted all of them. Rohit's aunt had her own theories about which month is "lucky". My head was spinning.
So Rohit said, "Let's just ask a real doctor." We booked an appointment with Dr. Kulkarni, a gynaecologist at the clinic near the station.
She was calm and kind. She asked about our health and history, suggested some routine tests, and talked through general habits. When I brought up the forum stuff, she smiled and said, "Bring your questions to me instead. Every person is different."
We came out with a printed sheet and a follow-up date. Rohit deleted two forum apps on the auto ride home.
I feel so much lighter.
— Aditi

qa.q: How did Aditi feel after the check-up, compared with before?
qa.a: Before, Aditi felt confused and overwhelmed by forum advice and relatives' theories; afterwards Aditi felt much lighter and reassured.

qa.q: What else could Aditi and Rohit do with the relatives' theories from now on?
qa.a: They could thank relatives politely and take any real questions to the doctor at the follow-up, rather than arguing over them.

qa.q: How might Rohit have felt deleting the forum apps?
qa.a: Rohit probably felt relieved and decisive, glad they now had a trusted professional to turn to instead of conflicting online advice.

grounding: It shows a couple booking a check-up with a gynaecologist for general preparation and following professional guidance instead of forums or relatives' theories.
